layers.label: 8. Apps
layers.summary: Programs that use the layers below and keep only their own rules.

layers.label: 7. Render, edit, sites
layers.summary: Showing notes to people: HTML rendering, the live editor, viewing chrome and site builds.

layers.label: 6. Query (later)
layers.summary: Reading a corpus as a database: loading records, queries, and JSON or SQLite builds.

layers.label: 5. Profiles (proposal)
layers.summary: Shared, versioned sets of types that many corpora can use, next to their own types.

layers.label: 4. corpus-schema
layers.summary: The spec for what a corpus declares about itself, and the validator that checks a corpus against it.

layers.label: 3. The corpus model
layers.summary: Every note in a corpus at once: files, links in both directions, frontmatter and tags, kept up to date.

layers.label: 2. Note parts
layers.summary: The pieces of one note: links, frontmatter, tags, tables and one document's structure.

layers.label: Data formats (proposal)
layers.summary: Lossless readers and editors for a file format in general, not just inside a note: YAML today, JSON later. Note parts build on them. Not one of the layers in docs/architecture.md yet.

layers.label: 1. Files
layers.summary: Walking folders, reading files and writing them safely. It does not know what Markdown is.

nodes.name: @osdlc/etag-write
nodes.purpose: Writes a file atomically and refuses to overwrite it if someone else changed it since it was read. Used to save notes without losing edits.
notes: Its tests live in the package. There is no shared conformance family for it yet.

nodes.name: etag-write
nodes.purpose: The Rust twin of @osdlc/etag-write: atomic writes with a hash check, so a stale write never replaces newer changes.

nodes.name: @osdlc/path-guard
nodes.purpose: Takes a path that came from outside (a request, a config file, a link in a note), joins it onto a root folder, and refuses it if the result could end up outside that root. It catches `..`, absolute paths, `~`, Windows drives and symlinks that point out of the root, and it works for files that don't exist yet. Anything that reads or writes files under a vault or corpus root uses it.
notes: It shares the path-guard conformance family with the Rust crate (packages/conformance/path-guard).

nodes.name: path-guard
nodes.purpose: The Rust twin of @osdlc/path-guard: the same lexical check and symlink-aware containment proof, run against the same conformance suite. markdown-vault-fs uses it for every file it touches.
notes: Open release PR osdlc/osdlc#730 would bump it to 0.3.4.

nodes.name: markdown-vault-fs
nodes.purpose: Walks a folder of notes: tells notes from attachments, applies the skip rules (including Obsidian's excluded files) and guards paths.
notes: Its name still says vault. Decision D1 says vault names move to corpus over time; the plan names no new name.
Open release PR osdlc/osdlc#730 would bump it to 0.6.1.
Open osdlc/osdlc#650 changes it (edge cases from earlier reviews). It still targets the branch of #648, which merged on 2026-11-08, and assumes 0.6.0 is unreleased, but 0.6.0 is on crates.io.

nodes.name: vfs-walk
nodes.purpose: A sorted walk of a folder tree through vfs-seam, with skip lists and a symlink policy. It knows nothing about Markdown.

nodes.name: vfs-seam
nodes.purpose: A file-access trait, so the same Rust code runs on a real disk, in memory or in a browser (WebAssembly).

nodes.name: @osdlc/markdown-link
nodes.purpose: Finds every wikilink, embed and relative Markdown link in a note body, and skips links inside code. Today it only finds links; it cannot say which file a link points to.
notes: Target: it gets the same link resolver as the Rust crate (LinkIndex), and becomes the only place in TypeScript that decides what a link points to (task 11).
Its shared test cases still live inside the package. Open osdlc/osdlc#728 moves them into a shared conformance family.
Open osdlc/osdlc#649 (0.9: more code forms) and #651 (link titles, parentheses in paths; stacked on #649) change both twins. #651 fixes problem F3 (osdlc/osdlc#635).
Problem F2: only the Rust crate can resolve links, so each TypeScript package wrote its own resolver.

nodes.name: markdown-link
nodes.purpose: Finds and resolves links in notes. Its LinkIndex resolves a link target against a set of file paths.
notes: The same open PRs change it: osdlc/osdlc#649, #651 and #728.
Open release PR osdlc/osdlc#730 would bump it to 0.8.2.

nodes.name: @osdlc/markdown-link (dev copy)
nodes.purpose: A private copy of markdown-link in the dev repo, at version 0.1.0. Several dev packages use it through workspace:* instead of the published 0.8.1.
notes: The plan names markdown-vault, vault-graph-core and markdown-astro as its users. dev's manifests show more: markdown-render, sdlc (solutions/ontological) and parts of determined also use it.
Problem F11. Task 13 moves its users off it. dev task T-1NC5 tracks the move and is marked in-progress/blocked.

nodes.name: @osdlc/markdown-tags (dev copy)
nodes.purpose: A private copy of markdown-tags in the dev repo, at version 0.1.0. dev's markdown-vault, markdown-render, markdown-editor and determined's notes experience use it through workspace:*.
notes: The plan does not mention this copy. It says markdown-tags moved into osdlc in osdlc/osdlc#714. It is shown as going away because it is an @osdlc package living in dev (problem F11) and the target has none.

nodes.name: @osdlc/frontmatter-lossless
nodes.purpose: Splits a note into its YAML frontmatter and body, and puts them back together byte for byte.
notes: Shares the frontmatter-lossless conformance family with the Rust crate, which is the reference.

nodes.name: frontmatter-lossless
nodes.purpose: The Rust twin of @osdlc/frontmatter-lossless. A broken frontmatter block is read as body only.
notes: Open release PR osdlc/osdlc#730 would bump it to 1.1.3.

nodes.name: @osdlc/markdown-tags
nodes.purpose: Finds inline #tags in a note body, in three dialects: Obsidian's rule (the default), a Unicode one and an ASCII one.
notes: Moved into osdlc in osdlc/osdlc#714. Shares the markdown-tags conformance family with the Rust crate.
The plan says markdown-tags is on neither registry yet. That is out of date: 0.4.0 is on npm and on crates.io.

nodes.name: markdown-tags
nodes.purpose: The Rust twin of @osdlc/markdown-tags, and the reference for their shared test cases.
notes: Open release PR osdlc/osdlc#730 would bump it to 0.4.1.

nodes.name: @osdlc/markdown-contract
nodes.purpose: Checks the structure of one document against a contract: its frontmatter, heading sections, tables, lists and code blocks. Then reads it as a typed model.
notes: Its shared test cases still live inside the package. The architecture plans a shared conformance family for it.

nodes.name: markdown-contract
nodes.purpose: The Rust twin of @osdlc/markdown-contract.
notes: Open release PR osdlc/osdlc#730 would bump it to 0.4.3.

nodes.name: markdown-contract 0.2.1 (vendored)
nodes.purpose: An old markdown-contract release, kept as a tarball in the dev repo. sdlc and several determined apps install it instead of @osdlc/markdown-contract.
notes: Also vendored at solutions/determined/vendor/markdown-contract-0.2.1.tgz. Its npm name, markdown-contract, is not on npm.
The plan does not mention it, so its target is unchanged here.

nodes.name: @osdlc/gfm-table
nodes.purpose: Reads, edits and renders GFM pipe tables as plain strings, and pads columns so the pipes line up.
notes: Its shared test cases still live inside the package. The architecture plans a shared conformance family.

nodes.name: gfm-pipe-table
nodes.purpose: The Rust twin of @osdlc/gfm-table.
notes: It is publish = false, so it is not on crates.io.

nodes.name: @osdlc/yaml-splice
nodes.purpose: Edits top-level YAML fields in place and keeps every other byte, comments included. It is the Rust crate built to WebAssembly for Node.js and Bun.
notes: It is a binding, not a twin: one crate built for another runtime, with no tests of its own.
It edits any YAML mapping, not only frontmatter. Frontmatter is its main use today: frontmatter-lossless splits the note, and yaml-splice edits the YAML part.

nodes.name: yaml-splice
nodes.purpose: Sets, removes and renames top-level YAML fields while every other byte stays as it was.
notes: Open release PR osdlc/osdlc#730 would bump it to 0.3.4.

nodes.name: yaml-splice-wasm
nodes.purpose: The WebAssembly wrapper that @osdlc/yaml-splice is built from.
notes: It is publish = false.

nodes.name: markdown-corpus
nodes.purpose: The corpus model in Rust: every note and file in a folder, their links in both directions, tags and frontmatter, kept up to date as files change.
notes: It never rejects a note: a note with broken frontmatter is read as body only.
Decision D3: the crate keeps its name, and the TypeScript model takes the same name.
Open release PR osdlc/osdlc#730 would bump it to 0.3.1.
Open osdlc/osdlc#650 changes it (see markdown-vault-fs).

nodes.name: markdown-relink
nodes.purpose: Moves or renames a note and rewrites the links that point at it, as a plan you can review before it is applied.
notes: Its code still says vault (VaultFacts).
Open release PR osdlc/osdlc#730 would bump it to 0.4.1.
Open osdlc/osdlc#651 also touches it.

nodes.name: @osdlc/markdown-vault
nodes.purpose: Reads an Obsidian-style vault from disk: each note's frontmatter, tags, links, embeds and backlinks. It has its own link-resolving rule.
notes: Version 0.2.2 in dev; not on npm.
Problems F1 and F4: it resolves links its own way, and says vault instead of corpus.
Task 12 merges it with vault-graph-core into the TypeScript markdown-corpus.

nodes.name: @sdlc/vault-graph-core
nodes.purpose: Builds a graph of notes and links from note data, with no file access. Its link resolver is a copy of the Rust one.
notes: Version 0.1.1 in dev; not on npm. Its scope is @sdlc, not @osdlc (problem F11).
Task 12 merges it with markdown-vault into the TypeScript markdown-corpus. Task 11 takes the TypeScript resolver from its copy of the Rust one.

nodes.name: @osdlc/markdown-corpus
nodes.purpose: The planned TypeScript corpus model: markdown-vault and vault-graph-core made into one package, built on markdown-link's resolver, the twin of the Rust crate.
notes: Decision D3 names it markdown-corpus.
The plan does not give a path. This follows osdlc/osdlc's packages/ts/<name> layout.
Its shared test cases are planned as a conformance family.

nodes.name: corpus-schema spec (SPEC.md)
nodes.purpose: The rules for what a corpus can declare about itself: a root file, type folders, record ids, record folders, JSON Schemas per type and typed links (x-ref). Its test cases sit beside it.
notes: Version 0 is in force (corpus-schema: 0). It has levels 0 to 2.
Near target: open osdlc/markdown#9 moves it here with its history. SPEC.md already says it moves once this repo has a release setup.
Proposals not built yet: a baseline and dialects (task 7), profiles through the extends key (task 9), and sharing whole corpora (tasks 27 to 30).
A plain-language guide is in this repo at docs/corpus-schema.md.

nodes.name: @osdlc/corpus-schema
nodes.purpose: The validator for the corpus-schema spec, as a library and the corpus-schema command. It checks records against their schemas, ids, links and typed references.
notes: 0.2.0 is its first version on npm. 0.1.0 was cut but never published (task 3).
Today it walks the folder and checks links itself (problem F8). Task 14 makes it read the corpus model instead.

Near target: open osdlc/markdown#9 moves it here with the same npm name, and open osdlc/markdown#10 builds and releases it with the shared osdlc workflows. Until those land, releases go out from osdlc/osdlc.
On the osdlc/markdown#9 branch its osdlc dependencies change from workspace:^ to npm ranges (^1.1.2 and ^0.8.1).
osdlc/markdown builds and releases it with the shared osdlc workflows, ts-packages-ci and ts-packages-release (task 21).

validate --fix exists today. Task 29 adds the corpus-schema sync command: it writes a read-only copy of inherited records into a generated folder, such as _inherited/org/, so Obsidian and GitHub links resolve. The validator then checks that the copy matches the pinned parent. Task 34 adds a move verb.

nodes.name: Rust corpus-schema validator
nodes.purpose: A planned Rust validator that runs the same conformance cases as the TypeScript one, built on the markdown-corpus crate.
notes: The plan names no crate. The architecture diagram places it in osdlc/markdown. The path is a guess at the repo's layout, not from a source.

nodes.name: claims example corpus
nodes.purpose: A valid level-2 corpus with the claims types: documents, methods, study-results and statements. Its records check a made-up claim about a tool called fernlog.
notes: The types follow GA4GH's VA-Spec 1.1.0 (decision D8). profiles/claims/README.md maps each type and field to VA-Spec.
Merged in osdlc/markdown#6. The plan still calls task 4 in progress.
People copy it with npx degit osdlc/markdown/profiles/claims/example. It is not on a registry.
profiles/claims/tests/ holds broken records that must fail with one expected error each.
Until task 31, evidence items are relative links with a pattern check, not x-ref.

nodes.name: @osdlc/corpus-profile-claims
nodes.purpose: The claims types published as a versioned profile, so a corpus names it under extends: and marks its types with x-extends instead of copying them.
notes: Decision D10 fixed the name, the folder and the prefix claims. The architecture still marks the profiles layer a proposal, and its open questions ask whether to adopt profiles.
Task 23 publishes it from this repo, after tasks 9, 21 and 31. If copies drift first, it could be released from osdlc/osdlc.
Not on npm.

nodes.name: acceptance-testing profile
nodes.purpose: A proposed profile built on claims: acceptance criteria are what statements are about, tests are methods and test runs are study results.
notes: The architecture diagram places it in osdlc/markdown. The plan gives no package name or path.

nodes.name: @osdlc/model-schema
nodes.purpose: The pack harness: loads packs (folders of YAML that declare kinds), compiles them, validates values and emits TypeScript types and JSON Schema.
notes: Only in open PR sksizer/dev#4069. It is not on dev main or npm.
Task 9 says model-schema moves to osdlc but does not name the repo. osdlc/osdlc is shown because the plan says packages stay there until they move to osdlc/markdown.
Decision D4 is open: profiles written as packs, or plain JSON Schema files that packs compile to. Problem F5: two ways to define types.
Packs differ from the proposed profiles: a record's own property replaces an inherited one, and strict can be overridden.

nodes.name: @osdlc/pack-intent and @osdlc/pack-sdlc
nodes.purpose: Two packs that port sdlc's 14 entity kinds (task, decision, principle and the rest) into the pack format.
notes: Only in open PR sksizer/dev#4070, stacked on #4069. The other package is at packages/ts/pack-intent.
The plan's levels-and-profiles diagram shows an sdlc profile with today's sdlc kinds. It does not say whether these packs become it, or where they live, so the target is unchanged here.

nodes.name: org principles corpus
nodes.purpose: A proposed shared corpus of an organization's principles. Project corpora extend it, refine some principles and waive others with a reason.
notes: The first real case for sharing across corpora. The plan does not say which repo holds it.

nodes.name: @osdlc/markdown-vault-query
nodes.purpose: Runs Obsidian Bases (.base) queries over a vault. In the target it becomes the one query layer, on top of the corpus model.
notes: Version 0.2.1 in dev; not on npm.
Problem F9: two query layers (this and a loader corpus-schema planned).
Task 15 moves it to osdlc on top of the corpus model. Its target name is not decided; the architecture keeps the word db for this layer, and decision D5 (what db means) is open.
Task 16 adds a build that writes every valid record to JSON files and a SQLite file.
The plan does not give a target path. This keeps its folder name in osdlc/osdlc.

nodes.name: @osdlc/markdown-render
nodes.purpose: Turns Markdown, including Obsidian's wikilinks, embeds, callouts and tags, into HTML, with Vue 3 components.
notes: Private in dev at 0.5.0; not on npm.
Near target: draft osdlc/osdlc#720 moves it to osdlc for a first release at 0.8.0, and finds links with @osdlc/markdown-link.
On that branch it reads the markdown-tags conformance cases.

nodes.name: @osdlc/markdown-astro
nodes.purpose: Brings an Obsidian vault into Astro content collections: rewrites embeds, copies assets and resolves wikilinks at build time.
notes: Version 0.1.0 in dev; not on npm.
osdlc/osdlc#719 moved it, but it merged into the branch of draft #720, not into main. The architecture still calls #719 open.
Problem F1: it resolves links its own way (resolveRef takes the first match and finds embeds by file name). Task 13 switches it to the shared model and resolver.

nodes.name: @osdlc/markdown-editor
nodes.purpose: An Obsidian-style live-preview Markdown editor on CodeMirror 6, with a Vue 3 wrapper.
notes: Private in dev at 0.5.1. Task 17 moves it to osdlc after osdlc/osdlc#719 and #720. There is no PR for it yet.

nodes.name: @sksizer/markdown-ui
nodes.purpose: Markdown viewing and editing chrome as a Nuxt layer: a surface that switches between reading, live editing and source.
notes: Private in dev at 0.6.0. It builds on @determined/ui.
Task 17 moves it to osdlc. There is no PR yet, and the plan does not say whether its @sksizer scope changes.

nodes.name: sdlc (@sdlc/cli)
nodes.purpose: The planning CLI and plugin. It keeps its planning docs as a corpus of notes with typed frontmatter.
notes: Uses osdlc note parts from npm, dev's private markdown-link copy, and the vendored markdown-contract 0.2.1. Its desktop app (solutions/ontological/desktop) uses the render and edit packages.
Target from the plan's diagram: it takes its types from profiles. Open sksizer/dev#4070 says sdlc does not use the packs yet.
Plan: nothing from dev is published.

nodes.name: determined
nodes.purpose: The plan calls it a notes app. In dev it is many small apps and experiences over a user's vault, such as notes, graph, search and sites.
notes: Uses the dev render, edit and corpus packages through workspace:*, plus osdlc note parts from npm and the vendored markdown-contract 0.2.1.
Task 13 switches its vault-graph app and its graph and notes experiences to the shared model and resolver.

nodes.name: skillwright
nodes.purpose: A CLI that publishes a vault of skill notes into the formats of coding-agent tools, checks them for drift, and edits and reorganizes the vault.
notes: Uses the osdlc Rust crates from crates.io, partly through its tradecraft-core crate.
Its workspace pins some older versions than the latest: markdown-corpus 0.2.0, markdown-relink 0.3.0, markdown-vault-fs 0.5.0, markdown-link 0.8.0.
It moved out of osdlc/osdlc into osdlc/skillwright.

nodes.name: harness-reference
nodes.purpose: A cited record of how coding-agent harnesses differ, kept as Markdown corpora, with its validators, an importer and a compiler for a knowledge file.
notes: Private package. It validates its beta corpus with @osdlc/corpus-schema ^0.2.0 from npm (osdlc/skillwright#95, 2026-11-09).
osdlc/skillwright#95 deleted skillwright's own markdown-db copy. The plan still lists that copy, and task 8 as not started.
Its compiled harness-knowledge.json feeds the draft @osdlc/harness-knowledge package (osdlc/osdlc#750).
Target: it uses @osdlc/corpus-profile-claims instead of copies (task 23).

nodes.name: harness-reference beta corpus
nodes.purpose: harness-reference's level-2 corpus: harnesses, subjects, and the claims types (documents, methods, study-results, statements) with harness fields added.
notes: osdlc/skillwright#97 (2026-11-09) moved it to the claims types: references became documents, evidence became study-results. Its schemas are copied from the claims example at commit 663f545. The plan still lists task 26 as not started.
The alpha corpus beside it has no root file and is not a corpus-schema corpus.
Open osdlc/skillwright PRs #98 and #100 to #106 add research records to it.

nodes.name: the evidence project
nodes.purpose: Another project that will keep evidence, observations and test material (scripts, queries, CSV results) as records with their files.
notes: The plan and architecture do not name it or its repo.
Task 5: it copies the types from the claims example and writes records, after tasks 3, 4 and 22. Task 23 switches it to the claims profile.

nodes.name: markdown-store
nodes.purpose: Reads and writes typed records as Markdown notes from Rust code, keeping the frontmatter lossless.
notes: publish = false, so not on crates.io.
Problems F6 and F7: it lays out records differently from corpus-schema, and has its own frontmatter and wikilink code.
Task 10: it writes the spec's layout and uses the shared note parts.
Where it lives in the target is an open question (stay in rust-ontogen or move to osdlc). Unchanged here.
Its Cargo.toml says it is meant to move into a rust-markdown workspace beside markdown-vault. The plan does not say this.

nodes.name: ontogen
nodes.purpose: A build-time code generator: from Rust structs it generates persistence, a store, an API and clients. Its Markdown backend writes records through markdown-store.
notes: Related crates on crates.io: ontogen-core 0.8.0, ontogen-macros 0.2.0, ontogen-jsonapi 0.3.0, ontogen-ts 0.2.0.
The plan does not say how its target changes beyond markdown-store (task 10).

dev's copy has the same five source files as osdlc's 0.8.1 but lacks its newer scan and size API, and eight dev packages and apps still link it.
dev kept a 0.1.0 copy of the same one-file package after osdlc moved it in (osdlc/osdlc#714) and published 0.4.0.
The tarball is the unscoped 0.2.1 build of the code osdlc now publishes as @osdlc/markdown-contract 0.7.7; the plan does not say to drop it.
vault-graph-core's resolve.ts is a hand port of the Rust LinkIndex and its tie-break, as its README says; task 11 moves the resolver into TypeScript markdown-link.
Both build the note and link graph in dev with different link rules: markdown-vault tries file names first, vault-graph-core indexes every path suffix (task 12 merges them).
markdown-vault's createLinkResolver decides what a link points to by its own rule (exact path, then file name, shortest path wins) instead of the shared resolver (problem F1).
markdown-astro resolves wikilinks with its own index where the first match wins, and embeds by bare file name (problem F1, task 13).
The validator walks the folder and builds its own wikilink index in validate.ts and links.ts instead of reading the corpus model (problem F8, task 14).
corpus-schema finds relative Markdown links with its own regex because markdown-link misses some (osdlc/osdlc#635, fixed by #651).
markdown-store's frontmatter.rs has its own split instead of the frontmatter-lossless crate (problem F7, task 10).
markdown-store's wikilink.rs parses and writes [[target#anchor|alias]] links itself instead of using markdown-link (problem F7, task 10).
markdown-store lays typed records out as <dir>/<id>.md with wikilink relations, while the spec uses type folders with schemas and relative links (problem F6, task 10).
markdown-store's walk.rs walks folders with the ignore crate instead of markdown-vault-fs; the plan only says it moves to the shared note parts.
Both define types and check records: model-schema with YAML packs and its own validator, corpus-schema with JSON Schema files and Ajv (problem F5).
The beta corpus's four claims schemas are copied from the claims example at commit 663f545 and extended, so the two drift apart until task 23.
markdown-render finds [[...]] and ![[...]] with its own regexes and uses markdown-link only for the attachment list; draft osdlc/osdlc#720 switches it.
